definitions.explanation: A person held captive as security for the fulfillment of certain conditions.

examples.japanese: {人質|ひとじち}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{解放|かいほう}→解放：00135_kaihou⟧⟦された→する：00392_suru⟧。
{人質|ひとじち}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{取|と}る→取る：00565_toru⟧。
{人質|ひとじち}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{安全|あんぜん}→安全：01131_anzen⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{確保|かくほ}→確保：13681_kakuho⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧こと⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{最|もっと}も→最も：01736_mottomo⟧⟦{大切|たいせつ}→大切：01456_taisetsu⟧だ。
examples.english: Ensuring the hostages' safety is the most important thing.

notes:
{人質|ひとじち} combines ⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧ (person) and {質|しち} (pledge/pawn/collateral). Literally "a person used as collateral."

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {人質|ひとじち}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{取|と}る→取る：00565_toru⟧: to take hostages
- {人質|ひとじち}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{解放|かいほう}する→解放する：22170_kaihousuru⟧: to release hostages
- {人質|ひとじち}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to hold someone hostage
- {人質|ひとじち}⟦{事件|じけん}→事件：01568_jiken⟧: hostage incident/crisis
- {人質|ひとじち}⟦{救出|きゅうしゅつ}→救出：12918_kyuushutsu⟧: hostage rescue
- {人質|ひとじち}⟦{交渉|こうしょう}→交渉：02727_koushou⟧: hostage negotiations

ETYMOLOGY:
In feudal Japan, {人質|ひとじち} referred to family members (often wives and children of feudal lords) held as guarantees of loyalty. This was a formal political practice, not a criminal act.
